name: The Humane League: policy, new commitments, volunteers and training
beneficiaries_note: Our build: animals, by share of the result at the defaults. New corporate commitments 'around the world' (53%) and the Open Wing Alliance members' wins (2%) spread by world population; grassroots pressure on switches at companies THL pressed, mostly in the US (38%, nine tenths US by the build's battery-cage share); state-law defence and the Animal Policy Alliance in the US (7%). A judgment.
summary: The Humane League's other programmes cost about $5.2 million in 2025, its programme spending less its grants and its accountability campaigns (two other lines): defending US state cage-free and crate-free laws against a federal override and supporting the Animal Policy Alliance's local campaigns, winning new corporate cage-free commitments (four companies, 1.6 million hens), mobilising volunteers and supporters to press companies to keep their commitments (7.5 million hens out of cages in the year), and training Open Wing Alliance members (216 new cage-free policies). The money is split by THL's annual report and ACE's 2024 breakdown, and each part is built from THL's own counts and the site's shared figures per hen, sow and meal; all five branches are discounted for missing data. Past wins count at THL's own next-dollar figure. The biggest uncertainties are how much grassroots pressure and training add to what companies and members would do anyway, THL's share among the groups behind its new commitments, and whether the 2025 opposition changed the chance that Congress overrides the state laws (one event, drawn as happens or doesn't, so the defence counts mainly at high risk settings).

rows.label: Open Wing Alliance training and coordination outside ACE's accountability costs, 2025
rows.explainer: Our judgment. THL's annual report (p. 17: Global Programs $5,204,000 (THL UK grant included, Open Wing Alliance grants not); Education & Mobilization $4,664,000; US Public Policy & Corporate Engagement $2,498,000; OWA & APA Grants $1,991,000; programmes $14,357,000 (preliminary, before audit)) leaves $3.05 million of global programmes after the THL UK grant, less than the larger of ACE's accountability blocks: most of the Alliance's team, summits and Fair and Fowl report sit in ACE's line, and the grants line's model of THL puts the whole at $1.5 million. What is left here is the trainings and mentoring outside that (four in-person Campaign Accelerators, 13 webinars, 19 campaign chats, 21 action parties, 27 mentees).

rows.label: Campaigns for new corporate commitments, 2025
rows.explainer: Our judgment. The annual report's US Public Policy & Corporate Engagement ($2.50 million, $2.54 million on the Form 990's total) less ACE's smaller accountability block ($1.65 million in 2025 prices) and the policy work above leaves about $0.2 million; global staff winning commitments abroad add some. Four new commitments in 2025 (1.6 million hens).

rows.label: Volunteers, grassroots mobilisation and their communications, 2025
rows.explainer: The remainder, mostly the annual report's Education & Mobilization ($4.66 million): organising THL's volunteers and supporters (about 1,300 changemakers, 6,180 actions and 1.48 million messages in 2025), protests, investigations and the communications that carry them, as far as ACE's accountability costs leave them out.

rows.label: SADs averted per animal-year, average of the branches (for reading only)
rows.formula: (new_sads_per_hen_year * new_outcome + trn_sads_per_hen_year * trn_outcome + vol_sads_per_hen_year * vol_outcome + def_sads_per_hen_year * def_sads_hens + def_sads_per_sow_year * def_sads_sows) / (new_outcome + trn_outcome + vol_outcome + def_outcome)
rows.explainer: Outcome-weighted average of the branches' figures, for reading only; each branch uses its own.

rows.label: Hens under members' pressed commitments helped by the training, relative to their new commitments
rows.explainer: Our judgment. The Alliance's training and strategy sessions also help members press companies to keep existing commitments (ACE's theory of change for the Alliance names both). Counted as a share of the new commitments' hen-years, before asking which would have switched anyway (the counterfactual below): from a fifth (most training is about winning new commitments) to as much again.

rows.label: Share of the animals under the laws that would go back into cages within the years counted if the laws fell
rows.explainer: Our judgment, the same as the grants line's model: in-state housing laws and company pledges would keep most cage-free and crate-free supply, and barns already built rarely go back to cages; replacement barns, buyers without pledges and price pressure after bird flu would bring some back.

rows.label: Chance a federal override of the state laws passes without the coalition's 2025 opposition

source.title: The Humane League, Animal Policy Alliance year in review (February 2026)
source.quote: By the end of the year, more than 200 members of Congress had signed letters opposing the EATS language

rows.explainer: Our judgment, the same as the grants line's model. The EATS Act's language and the 'Save Our Bacon' Act were in the House Farm Bill drafts of 2024-25 and the Department of Justice sued California over Proposition 12 in 2025; the coalition (Humane World for Animals, the ASPCA, THL and the Alliance's groups) gathered letters from more than 200 members of Congress against them (228, the annual report says, p. 6). Without that opposition we put an override in the next Farm Bill at 30%. One event, drawn as happens or doesn't.

rows.label: Chance it passes with the coalition's 2025 opposition
rows.explainer: Our judgment, the same as the grants line's model: the year's opposition takes about 5 points off (a sixth of the risk). Research on lobbying finds most campaigns change nothing (Baumgartner and colleagues, 2009); organised constituent contact moved legislators' support by about 12 points in a field experiment (Bergan and Cole, 2015). Drawn together with the chance without it.

rows.explainer: The site's one production response for diet change.

rows.label: Suffering in a US meal relative to the reference meal
rows.explainer: The site's US figure (docs/normalization.md 2.9): ACE's 2025 meal estimates put a US meal at 1.5 times the global one (0.75-3); the shared per-meal figure is a Latin American canteen meal.

rows.label: SADs averted per meal replaced
Share of new commitments that will later need accountability pressure
rows.explainer: Our judgment, the grants line's model's: the trackers and the Fair and Fowl report follow the larger companies, so about half the hens under a new pledge later get pressed. Later pressure is credited to later years' accountability, so a new commitment is credited only with what that pressure won't add (the template's recipe).

rows.label: Share of switches under pressed commitments that wouldn't have come yet without the pressure
rows.explainer: Our judgment, the grants line's model's, one question per switch: would it have come this year anyway? Many companies keep commitments without pressure (77% of due cage-free commitments are kept, the shared rate; 92% of the pressed ones THL tracks). Each switch credited counts the shared years.

rows.explainer: Our judgment, about the validity of the counts only (that the outcome isn't measured is the missing-data step): THL's count of hens under the four companies' commitments is its own, from the companies' egg volumes, and 'around the world' is unchecked.

Won commitments and defended laws push producers to convert barns that also supply buyers without a commitment, make further laws easier, and dearer cage-free eggs mean slightly fewer hens; investigations and protests reach the public (the 2025 egg-farm investigation reached 451 media outlets). Range 0-30%.

rows.label: Side effect: caged eggs and crated pork sold elsewhere, as a share of the animals' gain
rows.explainer: Our judgment. When a buyer or a state stops taking caged eggs, some of those eggs are sold to other buyers for a while, so fewer hens leave cages than the commitment covers. Range 0 to -25%.

rows.label: Side effects, net, as a share of the animals' gain
rows.explainer: The two side effects above, each read through the side-effects slider.
